lab.name: Visual Intelligence Lab @ Drexel
lab.description: We are a research group at Drexel University developing visual intelligence for humans and the physical world — spanning 3D humans, motion, and embodied AI; understanding people in real-world video; trustworthy biometrics and digital identity; and generative and multimodal AI, with impact in health, human performance, and education.

about.mission: The Visual Intelligence Lab at Drexel University is dedicated to pioneering research in computer vision, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. Our mission is to develop innovative technologies that advance the state-of-the-art in visual understanding and create meaningful societal impact.

research_areas.title: Physical 3D Human Digitization
research_areas.description: We develop methods for reconstructing and modeling humans in 3D from images and video, enabling applications in fitness tracking, healthcare, egocentric perception, and humanoid robotics.

research_areas.title: Generative AI & Deep Learning
research_areas.description: Our research focuses on building controllable and explainable generative models with applications spanning healthcare diagnostics, educational technology, and creative AI systems.

research_areas.title: AI for Social Good
research_areas.description: We leverage artificial intelligence to address critical challenges in healthcare, education, accessibility, and other human-centered applications that benefit society.

values: Mentorship and development of next-generation researchers
Ethical AI development with societal impact in mind

highlights.title: Physical Human Intelligence
highlights.description: 3D humans, motion, biomechanics, and embodied AI—modeling how people move and interact with the physical world.

highlights.title: Understanding People in Long, Real-World Video
highlights.description: Identity, activity, and evidence across long, multi-camera footage.

highlights.title: Trustworthy Biometrics & Digital Identity
highlights.description: Recognition, deepfake detection, and synthetic identity in a world of AI-generated media.

highlights.title: Generative & Multimodal AI for the Physical World
highlights.description: 3D generation, vision-language models, simulation, and domain generalization.

highlights.title: AI for Health & Human Performance
highlights.description: Interpretable, video-based digital biomarkers for how people move, change over time, and respond to intervention.

highlights.title: AI for Education & Scientific Learning
highlights.description: Multimodal AI that reasons about student thinking, instructional practice, and the evidence educators use.

research_directions.title: Physical Human Intelligence
research_directions.description: Modeling, understanding, and generating the human body, motion, and its interaction with the physical world, from images and video.

research_directions.title: Understanding People in Long, Real-World Video
research_directions.description: Persistently understanding who a person is, what they do, and how they change across long, multi-camera, real-world video.

research_directions.title: Trustworthy Biometrics and Digital Identity
research_directions.description: Creating, recognizing, and protecting human identity in a world increasingly populated by synthetic people, avatars, and AI-generated media.

research_directions.title: Generative and Multimodal AI for the Physical World
research_directions.description: Geometry-consistent, physically plausible, and controllable generation and multimodal reasoning over 3D, video, and language.

impact_areas.title: AI for Health and Human Performance
impact_areas.description: Interpretable, video-based digital biomarkers that quantify how a person moves, changes over time, and responds to intervention.

impact_areas.title: AI for Education and Scientific Learning
impact_areas.description: Multimodal AI that reasons about student thinking, instructional practice, and the evidence educators use to make decisions.

news.title: One paper has been accepted at SIGGRAPH Asia 2026! Congratulations to Yixuan and all co-authors!
VILab received a $25,000 Anthropic AI for Science Award to advance physics-grounded generative AI for organic crystal discovery, in collaboration with Dr. Matthew McDonald.
Dr. Liu received an Outstanding Researcher Award from the FAIR Center at Stanford University for our work on physics-grounded video analysis for interpretable gait assessment in DCM.
Our paper "BioGait-VLM" has been provisionally accepted at MICCAI 2026 (Acceptance rate: 9%). Congratulations to Anthony, Yuyang, and all co-authors!
Members of the VIL group attended NYC Computer Vision Day 2026 and presented a poster showcasing our latest research.
Two papers have been accepted at AIED 2026. Congratulations to Arijit, Yixuan and all co-authors (2x AIED)!
Congratulations to Dr. Liu for receiving two Drexel internal grants (2x Longsview Fellowship)!
Two papers have been accepted at CVPR 2026. Congratulations to Yuyang and all co-authors!
Dr. Liu is serving as an Associate Editor for IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security (T-IFS).
We are organizing the First PhysHuman Workshop @ CVPR 2026 (Denver), focusing on physically grounded human perception, modeling, and generation.
Received an NVIDIA Academic Grant Program Award, supporting our research on geometry-consistent, photorealistic driving-scene generation for autonomous driving.
Our paper "Person Recognition in Aerial Surveillance: A Decade Survey" is accepted by IEEE T-BIOM.
Dr. Liu was recognized as one of the ICCV 2025 Outstanding Reviewers.
Dr. Liu is serving as an Area Chair for CVPR 2026, ICLR 2026.
Our paper "HAMoBE" is accepted by ICCV 2025.
Dr. Liu is serving as an Area Chair for BMVC 2025, ACM MM 2025, FG 2025, IJCNN 2025.
Two papers, "SapiensID" and "AG-VPReID," have been accepted by CVPR 2025.
